One timeline, from twelve months out to two years home.

FOB's Path feature meets you wherever you are in transition — the app changes what it shows you based on your actual EAS date.

Start your TAP class with a plan

Understand what's ahead before mandatory transition briefings start, so you walk in with questions instead of leaving with more of them.

The Benefits Delivery at Discharge window — one of the most time-sensitive, least-understood steps in the whole process.

Everything translated, nothing oversimplified.

Six areas. One plain-language source, instead of six different offices.

Your Path
A personalized separation timeline built around your real EAS date and branch-specific TAP program.
Education
GI Bill and VR&E, explained side by side — so you know what actually fits your situation, not just what's available.
Housing
VA home loan eligibility and the zero-down-payment process, in the language a first-time buyer actually needs.
Documents
The paperwork that actually matters, and what each one is for — without the acronyms doing the explaining for you.
VA Claims Info
Plain-language 38 CFR lookups and a real combined disability rating calculator — calculated the way the VA actually does it.
More
Local events, veteran discounts, a working glossary, and crisis resources — always visible, never buried.

Built by someone who lived it.

I'm a Marine Corps veteran. When I got out, I didn't know what I'd earned, what I qualified for, or where to even start looking — and I don't think that's unusual. I think it's the default experience.

I built Future Operating Base mostly through vibe coding: fast, AI-assisted, iterative development that kept me close to the actual problem instead of buried in process. I'm not a trained engineer, and I'm not pretending to be one. I'm someone who needed this tool, so I built it.

It's free. It's staying free. And it's still very much in progress — which is exactly why your feedback matters right now, while it's still being shaped.

— Catherine Resoco, Founder
